name: consume-input-peak-memory

protocol.note: Both variants perform the identical real transform through compile()/submit() Stage 5 (ExecutionPlan::representation_requests). A standalone run_representation_transform never consumes (02 §4.2 / 06 §11: the adapter must not infer a destructive transform). multi-version-baseline sets consume_input=false: Stage 5 seals a RepresentationEpoch, publishes one target facet, reports old_backing_bytes>0 and released_backing_bytes==0, and retains the superseded linear backing alongside the new Private MTLTexture. consume-input sets consume_input=true with a complete ConsumeProof; Stage 5 then calls Arena::consume_representation (not Arena::consume): the allocation stays Active, its generation is unchanged, released_backing_bytes>0 and consumed_allocation_count==1, and the facet Stage 5 published still samples because the Private texture is distinct backing. An incomplete proof is rejected by ExecutionPlan::validate() before compile(). new_backing_bytes is the backend's own accounting (on Metal, MTLTexture.allocatedSize, which may exceed CanonicalView::byte_size() because of tiling/alignment); compare released_backing_bytes against old_backing_bytes rather than against the view's logical extent. submit() runs Stage 5 before the interpreter, so the compute module must name the post-transform representation_epoch (or load an allocation Stage 5 does not touch).

correctness.oracle: arithmetic: multi-version-baseline reports old_backing_bytes>0 and released_backing_bytes==0 (superseded backing retained); consume-input reports released_backing_bytes>0 and consumed_allocation_count==1, with the allocation still Active at the same generation; an incomplete ConsumeProof fails ExecutionPlan::validate()
correctness.tolerance: exact (integer byte counts, no floating-point involved). new_backing_bytes is not required to equal CanonicalView::byte_size().

fault_injection.reason: The catalog names 'fault before/during/after transform; capture replay request; external reference exists' as required fault-injection variants. The existing fault/poison mechanism (core::PoisonState/FaultRecord/ExecutionResult, ADR-005/ADR-009) is scoped to ir::Module instruction execution inside compile()/submit(). Reusing that mechanism for Arena-level consume_representation would invent a second, unrelated fault-injection concept. This milestone reports the row honestly as Deferred.

judgement: ConsumeInput is enabled only when the proof succeeds (ExecutionPlan::validate rejects an incomplete proof; the adapter never infers a destructive transform). The watermark claim is the released_backing_bytes vs old_backing_bytes delta on the Stage 5 path: multi-version retains the whole superseded backing, consume-input hands that backing back while the allocation and the newly published facet stay live. What is given up is replay/rollback to the pre-transform linear representation. Fault-injection coverage is explicitly Deferred, not silently omitted. No peak/steady byte counts are recorded here; those are measured by the vertical-slice driver on the host that runs it.
vulkan_status: compile-review-only (ADR-024/030); no Vulkan-side ConsumeInput wiring was attempted in this milestone (no Vulkan hardware reachable on this host, and this milestone's transform target -- SampleFacet -- is itself compile-review-only on Vulkan per E008)
